title: Unable to open BlueStacks 5 using CmdPal.

judgment.rationale: The attached CmdPal log captured access denied when AppCommand tried to start the BlueStacks .lnk directly, and the CmdPal app model already tracks the resolved executable path separately from the shortcut path.
evidence: The CmdPal log records AppCommand.cs::StartExe failing on BlueStacks 5.lnk with access denied.
The reporter added that .lnk files with extra startup parameters fail in both CmdPal and Flow Launcher.
Win32Program stores both LnkFilePath and FullExecutablePath, but AppCommand launches AppItem.ExePath directly.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a design pass that carries resolved shortcut targets and arguments into AppCommand, and validate it with a shortcut-with-arguments repro.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing linked fix covers CmdPal’s direct launch of .lnk entries that carry arguments.

issue_context.summary: CmdPal successfully indexes the BlueStacks shortcut, but launching it fails because the app command starts the raw .lnk path instead of the resolved executable + arguments path that the indexing layer already knows about.
known_information: Search indexing succeeds because the result appears in CmdPal.
The attached log shows access denied at AppCommand.cs::StartExe on the shortcut path.
The reporter added that the failing shortcuts rely on extra startup parameters.
inferences: The problem is in the launch path, not in search indexing.
Shortcuts with arguments are the highest-risk case because target and arguments must survive the model-to-command handoff.
issue_context.analysis: This is actionable without more reporter evidence. The current app model already exposes the safer launch data; the missing piece is the AppCommand handoff.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the issue body, maintainer bugreport request, attached bugreport ZIP, and reporter follow-up screenshot.
Reviewed CmdPal log entries showing AppCommand.cs::StartExe access denied on the .lnk path.
Reviewed AppCommand.cs, AppItem.cs, Win32Program.cs, and ShellCommand.cs.

comment.body: Approve a focused CmdPal shortcut-launch design pass for Issue 50196.

actions.label: Reproduce CmdPal .lnk launch failure
actions.note: Validate the launch path with a shortcut that carries arguments.

reproduce.version: PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 or newer current main build
prerequisites: Place a Start Menu shortcut that launches an executable with extra arguments.
Ensure CmdPal indexes the shortcut as an app result.
steps: Open CmdPal and search for the shortcut entry.
Invoke the result from the keyboard.
Observe whether AppCommand tries to start the .lnk path directly or launches the resolved executable target.
reproduce.expected_result: CmdPal should launch the shortcut target with its arguments instead of failing on the .lnk file itself.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Create a disposable shortcut to a known executable with one extra argument and add it to the Start Menu so CmdPal indexes it.

proposed_fixes.title: Launch resolved shortcut targets and arguments instead of raw .lnk paths
proposed_fixes.root_cause: CmdPal’s Apps extension preserves the original shortcut path as ExePath for display/identity, but AppCommand later uses that raw .lnk path for Process.Start. Shortcuts with arguments can therefore fail when starting the .lnk directly is denied or loses launch context.
plan: Carry the resolved executable path, parent directory, and shortcut arguments from Win32Program into AppItem.
Teach AppCommand to launch the resolved target through the existing ShellCommand helper instead of always starting AppItem.ExePath.
Retain a fallback to the original shortcut only when resolution data is unavailable.
verification: Reproduce with a shortcut that includes extra startup arguments and verify CmdPal launches the real target successfully.
Verify direct-executable and packaged-app launches still work unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The log shows the precise failing call site and the current model already has most of the data needed for a safer launch path.

design_decision.reason: Actionable design retained without full expansion.

confidence.rationale: Bugreport shows the failing call site and the current model already exposes the safer launch data.
